notes:
CRM notes:
- Mid-market SaaS building customer support + knowledge base assistant. Started w/Hosted API to move fast; POC showed promising latency.
- From PD: target SLO 250ms p95 for live traffic; peak throughput target ~350 requests/min (expected). Cost sensitivity: want clear uplift numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- POC learnings: hosted test had consistent p95 ~120ms on small sample, but they saw variable token counts (short chats + long doc excerpts). Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + quantization) to reduce unit cost.
- Primary ask now: Dedicated POC that proves canary strategy + automated fallback. They want documented plan: start 10% traffic to Dedicated variant A (full FP16 model) for 48h, increase to 50% if no perf/regressions, then 100% after week 2. Fallback rules: route to smaller model variant B (8-bit quant) on latency or cost threshold; region failover US-EAST -> EU-WEST for data-residency aware sessions; immediate rollback trigger if error-rate >1% or human QA failure.
- Security: SSO (SAML) mandatory, SOC2 + audit logs, customer-managed KMS, 90-day audit retention, EU residency for EU customers.
- SE notes: need to supply canary traffic generator, metric dashboards (latency by model variant, correctness regression via eval set), and an automated rollback playbook. SE action: Evan to draft canary runbook + routing policy by 2026-03-12.
- Procurement: waiting on final committed ARR bands; pricing deck shared (drive link). Procurement asked for sample committed capacity tiers and SLA language.
- Quotes from product lead: "Need deterministic inference economics — if Dedicated doesn't give predictable cost/LAT we can't commit."
- Quick wins: provide a Dedicated POC template, pre-populated canary thresholds, and a short eval harness (5k annotated prompts) they can run during the canary.
- Open items: finalize data residency for EU failover, SSO test account, confirm KMS key rotation policy.
